info.description: Hand-maintained. This document was generated by FastAPI while the server was Python; it is now a checked-in file (desktop/crates/server/src/openapi.json) served verbatim, because axum cannot enumerate its own router. get.description:
Capability (modality) map plus the resolved provider per capability.

Lets a client ask "who can do X" up front instead of discovering an
unsupported route via a failed request. ``resolved`` is the provider the
proxy would pick for an unqualified request of that capability (``null`` if
none is configured).

post.description:
OpenAI-style image generation, routed to a configured image backend.

Resolves an ``image_generation`` provider via the capability router: an
optional ``provider`` hint pins one, else the first configured image
backend is chosen. No image backend configured => structured 501.

OpenAI-style text-to-speech, routed to the configured speech backend.

The response body is audio, so it is returned as-is with the upstream's
content type rather than parsed. No speech backend configured => structured
501, which is what the desktop app reads as "use your own voice engine".

Single-turn chat completion via the embedded LLM proxy (POST {base}/chat/completions).
With ``stream: true`` the proxy's ``text/event-stream`` body is passed through
unchanged; otherwise the full JSON completion is returned.
Does not create a Process; for multi-agent runs use POST /api/v1/processes.

requests from simulated agents queue here instead of hitting the upstream at once.
The upstream call itself also retries on rate-limit responses (see upstream_http.py).

get.description: ADR 0008's amendment ("results, behind a key"): resolves the query exactly as GET /api/v1/search/dork does (ask=, q=, engine, site, filetype, drop, add_field/add_value all mean the same thing here), then, only when a search provider key is configured on this install, runs it and reads results back. The response is everything /search/dork returns (query, url, engine, source, recipes, parts, explanation, chips) plus three fields: `configured` (bool), `results` (array of {title, url, domain, snippet}), and `total_estimate` (integer or null). No key configured is the default install state, not an error: `configured` is false, `results` is an empty array, `total_estimate` is null, and every other field is populated exactly as /search/dork would answer it — an unconfigured install must not be told apart from a search that matched nothing by an empty `results` array alone, which is what `configured` is for. A key without a search-engine id (SEARCH_CX) is unconfigured the same way, not a partial configuration. `limit` caps how many results come back, default and maximum 10 — the search provider's own per-call cap, never paginated to fake a larger number (see `total_estimate` for that). A key Google rejects, or that has run out of its daily quota, is a real error distinct from `configured: false` and is answered with the provider's own message and a non-2xx status, not folded into the unconfigured response.

schema.title: Limit
schema.description: Capped at 10 regardless of what is asked for — the search provider's own per-call limit.

schema.title: Response Search Api V1 Search Get

400.description: Neither ask nor q was given, or add_field/add_value named an unknown field or failed that field's guard

schema.title: Response Search Api V1 Search Get 400

get.description: Translates a sentence (?ask=) or an already-written dork (?q=) into a Google dork query: the operator string, the ready-to-open URL, the parsed parts, one removable chip per part, and a plain-English explanation. q wins when both are given. Neither given is a 400. Optional engine (google|duckduckgo|bing, default google), site and filetype override or augment the translation. `drop` removes one piece already in the query before re-rendering — the exact token `render()` emitted for it (`site:reddit.com`, `filetype:pdf`, `-membrane`, `intitle:"Foo Bar"`); an unmatched `drop` is a no-op, not a 400. `add_field`/`add_value` are the inverse of `drop`: they add one operator to the query, built server-side (so the caller never spells dork syntax itself) and applied after `drop`, before the `site`/`filetype` overrides. `add_field` is a parts field name (`sites`, `exclude_sites`, `related`, `exclude`, `exact`, `any_of`, `intitle`, `intext`, `inurl`, `filetype`, `after`, `before`, `range`); `add_value` is the raw value (for `range`, `lo..hi` or `lo-hi`). Unlike `drop`, an unknown `add_field` or an `add_value` that fails that field's guard (whitespace in a domain, a non-numeric range) is a 400 naming the problem — a failed add would otherwise be the user's action doing nothing with no feedback. No outbound HTTP: this route calls at most this server's own /v1/chat/completions to translate ask= when the deterministic rules found nothing beyond plain terms. `explanation` mixes two row shapes, told apart by `kind`: `{kind: "recipe", label, meaning}` for a fired named intent (label is a recipe name like "document") and `{kind: "operator", label, meaning}` for a per-operator line (label is the operator string itself, like "site:reddit.com") — a recipe name is not an operator, so the two are never folded into one field. `chips` is one entry per removable element of `parts` — `{token, label, field}` — built server-side by `DorkQuery::chips` with the same grammar `drop` matches: `token` is handed back verbatim as `drop=`, `label` is the value with its operator prefix stripped for display, and `field` names the `parts` field it came from (`sites`, `exclude`, `exact`, `any_of`, `intitle`, `intext`, `inurl`, `exclude_sites`, `related`, `filetype`, `after`, `before`, `range`) so a client can choose a tone without parsing dork syntax; a grouped `(site:a OR site:b)` in the rendered string still yields one chip per site, never one per collapsed group. `parts.filetype` also accepts a pasted `ext:` dork on the way in (`DorkQuery::parse` treats `ext:` as a `filetype:` synonym) but `parts`/`query` always report the canonical `filetype:` spelling back.

get.description: This workspace's search history, newest first — every dork the app POSTed here, whether it was only built (opened=false) or actually run (opened=true). A workspace token sees only its own rows; the master key sees every workspace's. `limit` defaults to 50 and is capped at 200 regardless of what is asked for. `opened_only=true` restricts to rows that were actually run.

schema.title: Response List Search History Api V1 Search History Get

post.description: Records one dork the caller built or ran — {query, engine, source, opened}, all required except opened (default false). Not called automatically by GET /search/dork; the app posts explicitly, opened=false when a query is built and opened=true when the user runs it. Posting a query already on file for this workspace with opened=false and now opened=true promotes that row (flips the flag, bumps created_at) instead of inserting a near-duplicate; every other post inserts. Missing or blank query/engine/source is a 400.

get.description: How much of the machine the server may use right now, and how much of that is in use (ADR 0010). Read by the desktop sidebar monitor, which asks on the beat it already had rather than a timer of its own.

put.description: Sets the resource mode, or reports whether the user is at the window. Either field may be omitted and an omitted field is left alone, so the desktop can push a window event without restating a setting it did not change. Pushed on change, never polled. An unknown mode is a 400.

get.description:
Recent server log lines, one JSON object per line, newest last.

Poll with the `next` from the previous response to get only what has been written since. The
desktop shell has its own copy of this taken from the process's stdout — it covers startup and
crashes, which this cannot, because this only answers while the server is running.
